visual_appeal: Reduce the number of simultaneously prominent outlines. Keep the hero's 3 px state rail and the existing state colours, but make roster separators 1 px #443828 and secondary panel borders #594832. The portrait rims, chips, bars and panel edges currently compete for attention.

Establish three clear text tiers: primary content #EEE6D2, supporting information #C5BBA6, and section labels #CBB77D. Reserve bright gold for a small number of headings rather than distributing it across nearly every surface.
state_colours: Keep all four state colours, but enlarge roster chips from roughly 20 px to 24 px high and give their icons a consistent 6 px gap before the label. The red and orange labels are currently less comfortable to read than the green hero status.

In the compact tooltip, show an explicit state alongside each percentage, such as '21% · Resting' and '20% · Outside'. Currently the orange rows rely primarily on colour while the red row replaces its percentage with 'Outside', making comparison inconsistent.
Use the same inn icon for the Esc-card mover that appears on the actual Esc card. Its warning-triangle placeholder currently undermines the distinction introduced in the live alerts.
character_identity: Add the class to roster metadata, for example 'Lv 8 Warrior · Goldshire inn'. Keep class-coloured names and the settled portrait rules, but do not require users to identify a class from a small overlapping icon.

Move the character card's level badge into the metadata line. The saved-face portrait currently carries a level disc, class badge, state-coloured rim and sleeping glyphs; remove one attachment to make the face the clear focal point.

For saved looks, provide a nonmodal crop adjustment with a face-centre preview at the actual display size. Le Beouf's current enlarged crop is soft and tightly framed; a better source crop would improve identity more than additional portrait ornament.
default_theme: Reduce the default portrait's heavy gold surround to a 2 px bronze rim with a 1 px state-colour edge. Its current bright bevel is more visually dominant than the character name.
Darken the default roster surface toward #211B13 and reduce the contrast of its alternating brown areas. Preserve the theme's warmth, but bring its row hierarchy closer to the cleaner ElvUI version.

Keep the hero background artwork confined to the upper identity area and place a consistent dark scrim behind metadata. The forest detail should not compete with the small location and last-seen text.
elvui_wc3_fit: Retain the host frame art and blue button family. Within addon-owned content, use a consistent 14 px body font and 12 px section-label font; the current mix of large serif names and dense, heavily weighted small text feels less integrated than the supplied Character window.
Increase addon-owned action buttons from approximately 22 px to 26 px high, with 12 px horizontal padding. Keep their existing host styling rather than introducing another button treatment.
Give the addon canvas a consistent 12 px inset inside the host frame. Do not attempt to repair WC3 frame seams or Blizzard-owned Options chrome.
alerts_ux: In the logout banner, move the situation line below the complete instruction: 'Cancel logout, then hearth or find an inn.' Follow with the smaller 'Le Jette is outside a rest area.' The current headline and third line split one instruction around a status sentence.
Standardize the banner and Esc-card action label to 'View details', matching the main window. Use a 104 px minimum width and 26 px visual height while retaining the 32 px close hit targets.

In move mode, add a small dashed attachment indicator above the Esc-card placeholder, labelled 'Attached below Esc menu'. Keep the existing drag-to-detach explanation; the current isolated rectangle does not visually communicate its attachment.

Separate the toast trigger and recommendation by at least 6 px vertically. Keep the trigger amber and its rail red, but use cream for the recommended character name and green only for the full-rest status so the advice is not another competing warning.
readability: Raise roster metadata, ETA text, tooltip rows and Options helper text to at least 14 px at the normal scale. Several useful lines are currently compressed into approximately 12–13 px text while the surrounding panels have room to spare.
Show calendar completion consistently in the main roster, not only for the nearly-full character. Use a 64 px row with '21% · Full in 7d 21h' on one line and 'Wed 2 Dec, 01:36' below it in #C5BBA6.

Replace 'Full since 1d 16h ago' with 'Fully rested · reached cap 1d 16h ago'. The current wording combines 'since' with an elapsed duration and remains awkward even though it no longer resembles time remaining.

Reflow Options into a consistent label-and-control grid with 24 px checkbox rows and 20 px gaps before section headings. Move parenthetical explanations onto indented helper lines instead of making long checkbox labels carry the entire explanation.
layout_polish: Recompose the saved-look card's upper area into a 160 px portrait column and a flexible text column containing speech, name and metadata. The current upper-left speech bubble and upper-right face leave a large disconnected central void.

Move the hero's runner-up line beside or below the main recommendation, not beneath the banked-level metric at the far right. It belongs to the play order, whereas its current placement makes it resemble a qualifier on the 1.5 value.

Clarify the timeline's visual grammar. Label it 'Time until full', use 4 px duration tracks with distinct endpoint markers, and keep current percentages in a fixed column. Equal-length orange tracks otherwise resemble equal progress despite their different completion dates.
Reduce night-band opacity and make them neutral, such as #333333 at 45%. In the supplied timeline they still read as large slate blocks and overpower the thin row structure.
Give the timeline's AFTER 48H column at least 132 px and show the completion time on a second line. Preserve the endpoint arrows, but do not reduce a precise completion estimate to a date alone.
delight: Bring the hero's speech treatment and character card into the same visual family: identical 12 px bubble padding, a 1 px bronze edge and a consistent tail. Currently one feels like a small label and the other like a separate large panel.

Keep the character-specific speech, but let the saved-look portrait sit closer to the bubble so the line clearly belongs to that character. Spatial connection will add more personality than more badges or stronger glow.

In compact mode, add a 6 px gap after each state group and show counts in the hover header. The current uninterrupted run of coloured pips is functional but reads more like a diagnostic strip than a polished miniature roster.

overall_notes: A substantial improvement over the real baseline: the recommended character is unmistakable, the button families are coherent, and the alerts now communicate useful actions without modal interruption. The design is good, but I would not yet approve it as best-in-class. Its remaining weaknesses are small-text density, too many equally emphatic borders, an under-composed saved-look card, and timeline semantics that require interpretation. The strongest next pass is subtraction and alignment, not additional ornament or features. I have not deducted for simulator model placeholders, inline class-colour limitations, settled portrait rules, or host-owned WC3 and Options artifacts.
